ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image there is a circle, and a square is inscribed in the circle; the bottom side of the square is labeled 10 in., and there is a diagonal from the upper-left vertex to the lower-right vertex passing through the center of the circle. Because the square is inscribed in the circle, this diagonal of the square is the diameter of the circle. The side length of the square is 10, therefore the diagonal d = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(200) = 10sqrt(2). The circumference of the circle C = pi*d = 10pi sqrt(2).

raw_record.question_text: Find the exact circumference of each circle.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: a square is inscribed in the circle, the bottom side of the square is labeled 10 in., and a diagonal of the square runs from the upper-left vertex to the lower-right vertex through the circle’s center. Treat that diagonal as the circle’s diameter. Use the side length 10 of the square and the Pythagorean theorem to find the diagonal: d = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = 10sqrt(2). Then apply the circumference formula C = pi*d to get 10pi sqrt(2).
